{"self_assessment": "Impact
I proposed the fish at the start of the round and sketched it on the pad: one line over the back, one under the belly, crossing into a tail. That design gave the table a clear, simple outline that could be built as one connected run. The table ended with 112 standing dominoes, all connected to the start, so the whole picture was set up to fall in a single push.

Execution
I traced stroke 2, the belly line, from the nose all the way to the tail tip, and I laid the start domino as part of that. I inspected the tail crossing closely, twice, and flagged that the join was turning too sharply so it could be corrected before the push. I then kept my hands off the finished work, since a bump was the bigger risk by then.

Collaboration
I split the work cleanly: Priya took the top line, I took the belly, and Maya and Tom kept the bin stocked and checked the joins. I kept everyone updated on progress at the crossing, offered to take over the last stretch of the top line when it lagged, and accepted Maya's offer to finish it. Throughout, I made it easy for people to ask for or offer help.

Leadership
I set the plan in the first seconds: the animal, the shape, who builds which stroke, and who supplies dominoes. I kept the table coordinated through the build and called the hands-off decision once the run connected, which kept the finished picture intact for the push. The result was a recognizable fish, fully connected from nose to both tail tips.", "my_share_percent": 35}
